title: Views above La Silla
caption: The Milky Way and the Magellanic Clouds above La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The glow of the Milky Way and the two Magellanic Clouds hangs above a pair of telescopes at ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile. ESO says the skies over this site offer some of the most spectacular views anywhere.

Three galaxies share this sky. The Milky Way is our own, seen from the inside as a band of light formed by countless distant stars. The Large and Small Magellanic Clouds are separate, smaller galaxies, dwarf companions of the Milky Way that appear as separate hazy patches.

From the Southern Hemisphere, the Magellanic Clouds are a familiar feature of dark skies. Because they are so close to us, astronomers can study their stars and gas in far more detail than they can in more distant galaxies.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at La Silla. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: The Magellanic Clouds can be seen with the naked eye under dark skies, but a long exposure shows them, and the Milky Way, brighter than they would appear in person.

explore: Dark, clear skies like those at La Silla let a camera capture the soft glow of neighbouring galaxies. Here, two of La Silla's telescopes sit beneath all three galaxies at once.
alt: The Milky Way and two hazy cloud-like galaxies in the night sky above two telescopes.
